1. Introduction

This paper develops a layered theory of artificial intelligence systems, in which cognitive functions are modeled as nested computational abstractions (from low-level perception [through symbolic inference {to strategic planning}]) and evaluated under a unified formalism. The proposed schema, (((([[[[[{{{{{AI}}}}}]]]]]])))) , nests five parentheses, five brackets, and five braces to indicate that model, data, and inference are not separate artifacts but recursively embedded constraints. We argue that this nested representation clarifies how machine-learning systems combine statistical abstraction, relational reasoning, and goal-directed adaptation, and we present a benchmark framework for assessing these capacities across generative and symbolic AI architectures.
